verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission launch is on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Published: March 31, 2026 ... tomorrow, April 1'; R6: 'Updated on: April 1, 2026'; R3 URL: '/2026/04/01/live-artemis-ii-launch-day-updates/'; R1: 'launch countdown live on April 1'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state or imply April 1, 2026, as the launch date, with R4 and R6 explicitly including the year.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II launch is scheduled for roughly 6:35 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'liftoff at a T-0 time of 6:35 p.m. EDT'; 'lifted off ... at 6:35 p.m. EDT'; R5: 'lifted off ... at 6:35 p.m. ET'; R2: '6:24 p.m. EDT ... two-hour window'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm exact liftoff time of 6:35 p.m. EDT within the window starting at 6:24 p.m., matching 'roughly 6:35 p.m.' precisely.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a 10-day mission around the moon and back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'roughly 10-day deep space excursion ... slingshotting around the moon'; R3: 'approximately 10-day Artemis II mission around the Moon'; R4: '10-day mission looping around the Moon and back'; R2/R5: 'return in 10 days'; R6: 'nine-and-a-half-day voyage around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: All sources describe a ~10-day mission looping around the moon and back, with minor variation in R6 but directly supportive.

verifications.claim: NASA’s AROW is the Artemis Real-time Orbit Website.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: R4 directly states the full name and acronym match exactly.

verifications.claim: NASA’s AROW provides live tracking of the Orion capsule's journey.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'NASA’s Artemis Real-time Orbit Website (AROW) lets you follow Orion’s journey around the Moon as it happens ... displays Orion’s location ... distance, speed, altitude'
verifications.reasoning: R4 explicitly describes AROW providing real-time tracking of Orion's position and journey data.
